Scoring children

Source: vignettes/pediatric-scoring.Rmd
pediatric-scoring.Rmd

score_le8() scores children aged 4 months to 19 years with the pediatric Life’s Essential 8 (LE8) definitions from the American Heart Association’s 2022 advisory: the children column of its Table 1, and the suggestions for younger children in its Supplemental Appendix 2. Adults and children can be scored in the same call; each row’s age chooses the definitions, and le8_population records which were used.

This article covers what changes for children, which inputs to supply, and how to derive growth-chart and blood-pressure percentiles.

library(essential8)
library(dplyr)

What changes for children

Each component uses an age-appropriate rule. Some are defined only from a certain age; before then, the component is NA and does not count toward min_components.

Component Pediatric rule Ages scored
Diet MEPA from the same columns as adults: 6 items (6-23 months), 10 items (2-5 years), all 16 (6-19 years); or population percentiles 6 months+ (percentiles: 2 years+)
Physical activity Daily active play (1-5 years); weekly moderate or vigorous minutes, not doubled (6-19 years) 1 year+
Nicotine exposure Never tried, tried over 30 days ago, current inhaled NDS, current combustible; secondhand smoke at any age All
Sleep Distance from the age-appropriate range (12-16 h at 4-11 months to 8-10 h at 13-19 years) All
BMI WHO weight-for-length percentile and rapid gain (under 2); CDC BMI percentile and % of 95th percentile (2-19 years) All
Blood lipids Pediatric non-HDL bands (<100, 100-119, 120-144, 145-189, 190+ mg/dL) All
Blood glucose Same as adults All
Blood pressure AAP 2017 percentile categories (1-12 years); adult bands (13-19 years) 1 year+

AHA suggests that the composite for a child be the average of whatever components are available and appropriate for measurement. Laboratory values are often unavailable in children, and the NHANES analysis that accompanied the advisory averaged as few as three components, so pediatric analyses usually set min_components below the default of 7.

A preschool child

Children use the same MEPA columns as adults. At ages 2-5, ten of the items are scored, at 10 points per item met, with child-sized thresholds:

  • vegetables: green_leafy_vegetables + other_vegetables, 2+ per day
  • fruit: berries + other_fruit, 14+ per week (2 per day)
  • whole_grains 3+ and olive_oil 1+ per day
  • fish 1+ and nuts 4+ per week
  • meat, butter_cream, and sweets_and_pastries 3 or fewer per week; for children under 6, sweets should include sugar-sweetened beverages
  • fast_food 2 or fewer times per month (at most 24/52 per week)

chicken, cheese, beans, alcohol, and sex are not used before age 6 and may be omitted from data containing only young children.

The example also uses active play in minutes per day and blood-pressure percentiles. The 90th and 95th percentiles (systolic_bp_p90 and so on) are the child’s reference values for age, sex, and height, in mm Hg.

preschooler <- tibble(
  id = "preschooler",
  age = 4,
  # Servings per day
  green_leafy_vegetables = 1,
  other_vegetables = 1,
  whole_grains = 2,
  olive_oil = 1,
  # Servings per week
  berries = 7,
  other_fruit = 14,
  sweets_and_pastries = 2,
  meat = 2,
  fish = 1,
  nuts = 2,
  butter_cream = 1,
  # Times per week
  fast_food = 0.25,
  active_play_minutes = 160,
  smoking_status = "never",
  current_inhaled_nds = FALSE,
  secondhand_smoke_home = FALSE,
  sleep_hours = 13.5,
  bmi_percentile = 60,
  bmi_percent_of_p95 = 82,
  systolic_bp = 108,
  diastolic_bp = 60,
  systolic_bp_p90 = 103,
  systolic_bp_p95 = 107,
  diastolic_bp_p90 = 63,
  diastolic_bp_p95 = 67,
  antihypertensive_treatment = FALSE
)

preschooler |>
  score_le8(min_components = 5) |>
  select(mepa_total, starts_with("le8_"))
#> Warning: ! Some LE8 components could not be calculated for any observations.
#> ✖ Blood lipids
#> ✖ Blood glucose
#> ℹ Overall LE8 composite scores will use the available components, subject to
#>   `min_components`.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   mepa_total le8_diet_score le8_physical_activity_score le8_nicotine_score
#>        <int>          <dbl>                       <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1          8             80                          90                100
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: le8_sleep_score <dbl>, le8_bmi_score <dbl>,
#> #   le8_blood_lipids_score <dbl>, le8_blood_glucose_score <dbl>,
#> #   le8_blood_pressure_score <dbl>, le8_n_components <int>,
#> #   le8_composite_score <dbl>, le8_complete <lgl>, le8_category <chr>,
#> #   le8_population <chr>

Eight of the ten items are met (80 points); mepa_total counts items met on the screener for the child’s age. Sleep is half an hour above the 10-13 hour range (90 points). The systolic pressure of 108 mm Hg is at or above this child’s 95th percentile (107 mm Hg) but below 95th + 12 mm Hg, which is stage 1 (50 points). Lipids and glucose were not measured, so the composite averages six components; the warning says so.

Infants and toddlers

From 6 to 23 months, diet uses six items: vegetables, fruit, and whole grains (at least once a day before 12 months, twice a day from 12 months), no sweets or sugar-sweetened beverages, no fast food, and the milk source recommended for age. milk_source is the one column used only at these ages: "human", "cow", "formula", or "other". Human milk meets the item before 12 months, and human or cow’s milk from 12 months.

Weight uses the WHO weight-for-length (or BMI-for-age) percentile together with the change in its z-score since the prior routine visit. An increase of 0.67 or more counts as rapid weight gain.

infant <- tibble(
  id = "infant",
  age = 0.75,
  age_months = 9,
  green_leafy_vegetables = 0.5,
  other_vegetables = 0.5,
  berries = 3,
  other_fruit = 4,
  whole_grains = 1,
  sweets_and_pastries = 0,
  fast_food = 0,
  milk_source = "human",
  smoking_status = "never",
  current_inhaled_nds = FALSE,
  secondhand_smoke_home = TRUE,
  sleep_hours = 13,
  infant_weight_percentile = 98.5,
  infant_weight_z_change = 0.4
)

infant |>
  score_le8(min_components = 4) |>
  select(mepa_total, starts_with("le8_"))
#> Warning: ! Some LE8 components could not be calculated for any observations.
#> ✖ Blood lipids
#> ✖ Blood glucose
#> ℹ Overall LE8 composite scores will use the available components, subject to
#>   `min_components`.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   mepa_total le8_diet_score le8_physical_activity_score le8_nicotine_score
#>        <int>          <dbl>                       <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1          6            100                          NA                 80
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: le8_sleep_score <dbl>, le8_bmi_score <dbl>,
#> #   le8_blood_lipids_score <dbl>, le8_blood_glucose_score <dbl>,
#> #   le8_blood_pressure_score <dbl>, le8_n_components <int>,
#> #   le8_composite_score <dbl>, le8_complete <lgl>, le8_category <chr>,
#> #   le8_population <chr>

age_months is optional; when supplied it sets the pediatric age bands more precisely than age * 12. Physical activity and blood pressure are not scored before age 1, so they are NA here regardless of the inputs.

School-age children and adolescents

From age 6, diet uses all 16 MEPA items and the adult bands, so sex (for the alcohol item) is needed from this age. Weekly moderate and vigorous minutes count once each (adults count vigorous minutes twice). The pediatric nicotine categories describe any nicotine product: "never" means never tried, "former" means tried but not within 30 days, and "current" means combustible use within 30 days. Blood pressure switches to the adult bands at 13, while the other components stay pediatric through age 19.

Deriving growth-chart and blood-pressure percentiles

add_pediatric_references() derives the percentile inputs from raw measurements, using the suggested packages cdcanthro (CDC and WHO growth charts) and pedbp (AAP 2017 blood-pressure percentiles). It needs sex, height, and weight, and uses age_months or age * 12.

measurements <- tibble(
  id = c("toddler", "school_age", "teen"),
  age = c(1.5, 8.25, 15.5),
  sex = c("male", "female", "male"),
  height_cm = c(82, 128, 172),
  weight_kg = c(11.5, 27, 64)
)

measurements |>
  add_pediatric_references() |>
  select(id, bmi_percentile, bmi_percent_of_p95, infant_weight_percentile,
         systolic_bp_p90, systolic_bp_p95)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   id    bmi_percentile bmi_percent_of_p95 infant_weight_percen…¹ systolic_bp_p90
#>   <chr>          <dbl>              <dbl>                  <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1 todd…           NA                 NA                     76.3            99.7
#> 2 scho…           60.9               78.8                   NA             110. 
#> 3 teen            68.5               79.6                   NA              NA  
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​infant_weight_percentile
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: systolic_bp_p95 <dbl>

Blood-pressure references are returned only for ages 1 to 12, and only when height is known: without height, pedbp would assume a median-height child, which is a form of imputation the package avoids.

Rapid infant weight gain compares visits, so it cannot be derived from one row. With longitudinal data, compute it from infant_weight_z within each child:

visits |>
  add_pediatric_references() |>
  arrange(child_id, age) |>
  mutate(
    infant_weight_z_change = infant_weight_z - lag(infant_weight_z),
    .by = child_id
  )

AHA compares against the z-score at prior routine visits, for example since age 1 month; choose the comparison visit to match your study design.

Where the sources conflict

The advisory’s main table and its supplement are not always consistent. The package follows the more specific rule and documents each choice in ?score_le8:

  • Ages 2-5 use the supplement’s 10 points per item met rather than Table 1’s banded 0-10 scale (for example, 7 items score 70 rather than 80).
  • The supplement calls the 16-item MEPA the screener “used in older children and adults”, so ages 6-19 use it with the adult bands.
  • At 6-23 months, weight at or above the 99.7th percentile with rapid gain scores 0, the supplement’s explicit worst state, rather than the 25 its listed decrements would give.
  • Nineteen-year-olds use the 13-18 year sleep range (8-10 hours), the last range AHA lists for the pediatric column.
  • The packaged NHANES diet references describe adults, so they are refused for children. Use percentiles in diet_value or a pediatric reference.
